evidence: All 19 save_load tests pass including the new `legacy_schema_v2_saves_with_unseeded_tracker_reseed_stability_baselines` regression test (cr7 amendment) and both pre-existing tracker tests (`legacy_schema_v2_saves_without_tracker_reseed_stability_baselines`, `legacy_schema_v2_saves_are_migrated_to_net_water_volume`).
All 10 shrimp_population tests pass including the rewritten deterministic `hatch_produces_juveniles`.
`cargo clippy -p tank_core --tests -- -D warnings` passes with no warnings.
`cargo fmt -p tank_core -- --check` passes with no formatting issues.

MigrationFn signature is `fn(&mut Value) -> Result<(), SimError>` (save.rs:33) with dedicated `SimError::SchemaMigration { from, to, message }` variant (actions.rs:83-84) and structured helpers (`required_f64_at`, `required_positive_f64_at`, `required_array_at`, `required_object_mut_at`, `schema_migration_error`).
Compile-time assertion at save.rs:89-92 ensures `MIGRATIONS.len() == SCHEMA_VERSION - MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA`, preventing silent version/migration count drift.

Migration contract is comprehensively documented at save.rs:41-76 with 5 numbered steps, 'what migrations can do' section, and 'ordering guarantees' section — satisfying the acceptance criterion for documented migration path.

`reconcile_stability_tracker` (save.rs:351-366) now receives `source_schema_version` and delegates to `has_unseeded_legacy_stability_tracker` (save.rs:372-376) which correctly scopes the reseed to schema-2 saves where the tracker equals `StabilityTracker::default()` but does not match the migrated water state — preserving valid historical trackers from later schemas.

The regression test at save_load.rs:234-271 constructs a schema-2 payload with `StabilityTracker::default()` sentinel, loads it, verifies baselines are reseeded to match migrated water state, and then runs `update_stability_tracker` to confirm the first daily pass produces zero instability.
`SchemaVersionTooOld` error (actions.rs:78-81) now includes user-facing remediation text: 're-create this save with a newer version of the application'.
`SchemaVersionTooNew` error (actions.rs:73-76) provides corresponding guidance: 'upgrade the application to load this save'.
Schema version is restamped per migration step (save.rs:169) for crash-safe intermediate versioning.

migrate_v2_to_v3 validates geometry positivity (`required_positive_f64_at`), rejects negative substrate depths, validates substrate depth <= fill height, and requires positive net water volume before rescaling dissolved totals — all returning explicit `SchemaMigration` errors.

The `stability_tracker_matches_water` helper (save.rs:378-395) uses 1e-9 tolerance comparisons across all four baseline fields, which is appropriate given f64 arithmetic and avoids false negatives from floating-point noise.
findings_or_gaps: The `test_closed_system_shrimp_reproduction_conserves_n_and_c` test in budget_tracking.rs fails on a pre-existing assertion ('expected deterministic hatching to occur'). Verified this failure exists on the base state with no local changes — it is not a regression from this deliverable.

The pre-existing `enforce_invariants(&mut self.state)` mutation-on-error architectural issue in engine.rs remains. Normalization clamps execute before hard validation, so a rejected step can still modify live state. Unrelated to save-schema work.

The `has_unseeded_legacy_stability_tracker` check at save.rs:373 is scoped to `source_schema_version == 2` only. If a schema-3 save ever had an uninitialized tracker (e.g., from a bug in an intermediate version), it would not be caught. However, schema-3+ saves were created after tracker seeding was added to the creation path, so this scoping is appropriate.
follow_up_or_amendments: The `test_closed_system_shrimp_reproduction_conserves_n_and_c` failure in budget_tracking.rs should be investigated separately — either the test fixture's hatching assumptions need updating or the reproduction logic has an unrelated regression.
The enforce_invariants mutation-on-error issue should be addressed in a separate task by splitting pure validation from normalization or validating against a clone.
